title: Data-contract sidecar
description: The AUTHORED half of the data contract (Phase 1 / WP 1.2). One file per table in supabase/contract/<table>.contract.yaml. The introspected half (build/schema.introspected.json) says what the schema IS; a sidecar says what each column MEANS, what unit it carries, which engine code reads it, and what the user typed to produce it. WP 1.4's generator merges the two; its checker fails when either describes something the other does not.

$reserved.$comment: Declared now, used by nothing yet. Reserving costs a line; retrofitting costs a UI pass (PLAN.md §8 WP 1.2 step 3).
$reserved.schema_name.observations: The Postgres schema tier 2-O will live in. Nothing writes it yet.
$reserved.provenance.estimated: A value fitted by an estimator from observations rather than asserted. Phase 7+.
$reserved.provenance.contract: A value the data contract itself supplies — the declared default, not a guess. Phase 6.
$reserved.field.grain.rate: A quantity per unit time (a flow). Needs `unit` to name the period.
$reserved.field.grain.event: One timestamped occurrence rather than a standing level. Tier 2-O.

schema_name.description: Postgres schema. 'observations' is reserved for tier 2-O.

grain.description: What ONE ROW is, in the user's terms. Not the primary key — the thing.

owner.description: Which part of the system is responsible for the rows being correct. `analysis` (WP 4.2) is the analyses that produce derived metrics — distinct from `etl`, which is `combine-project`'s graph build, and from `engine`, which is the simulation. It was added rather than folding the analysis store into `etl`, because labelling the owner wrongly in the table that exists to end mislabelled provenance (D19) would be a poor trade for one enum value.

natural_key_unique.description: Uniqueness the table ACTUALLY has, copied from build/schema.introspected.json. Record it truthfully even when it is wrong: the four lane tables have only `id`, which is D5, and WP 3.3 fixes it.

natural_key_intended.description: The key the grain implies, where the table does not yet have it. Present ONLY when natural_key_unique fails to enforce the grain; WP 3.3 lands these as constraints. Never a claim about today.

read.description: capability key from public.capabilities, or null for 'any project member'

write.description: capability key; null means no user-facing write path exists

min_project_role.description: WP 2.2's project_members.project_role vocabulary. Forward-declared: project_members does not exist yet.

audited.description: I-G4: does a tier transition on this table write an audit row naming the actor? Today this is false almost everywhere; WP 2.3 is where it becomes true.

rls_enabled.description: Copied from introspection. A tier-2 table with rls_enabled false is a finding.

fields.description: Every column of the table, no exceptions. WP 1.4's checker fails on a column with no entry and on an entry with no column.

ingest_dataset.description: WP 3.2. Present when a CSV UPLOAD targets this table, and it is what makes the upload contract-driven rather than hand-written: `ingest-file` builds its parser and its validator from the generated spec, never from a list in the function. Absent means the table has no CSV origin.

wizard_id.description: The template id UploadWizard offers, so one name spans the button and the run.

fact_class.description: What kind of fact one row is — the `ingest_staged_rows.fact_class` value. Structure (a BOM) is master; a quantity over a period (a lane) is transactional.

server_set.description: Columns the SERVER supplies from the project and the CSV may never carry. A file that names one is refused rather than trusted.

analysis_kinds.description: WP 4.2 · §11's OPEN ENUM with its params schema. `analysis_kind` is a TEXT column whose CHECK constrains the shape only, so a new kind costs a sidecar edit and not an `ALTER TYPE`, a migration and a deploy. The catalog of kinds is a data fact and `single-source` (I1) says a data fact is authored exactly once — here.

computed_by.description: The analyzer that produces this kind.

params.description: Each parameter's type, default and meaning. A default declared nowhere is `declared-fallback` (I6) broken.

surfaces.description: TABLE-GRAIN lineage (WP 5.1): which pages reach this table, by what path, with a file:line a reviewer can open. It does NOT claim that every column is rendered on those pages — that claim needs column grain, and a field's own `surfaces` carries it where the evidence exists.

unit.description: The physical unit. null for dimensionless, identifiers and text.

unit_source.description: Where the unit comes from. 'fixed' — the contract fixes it and the CSV cannot change it (inbound_logistics.lead_time is weeks, full stop). 'column' — another column of the same row names it (volume, via time_unit). 'derived' — it follows from the units of the inputs. 'none' — dimensionless.

normalize_at_promotion.description: WP 3.3 (invariant I3) — how this value is converted into a canonical unit as it is PROMOTED into tier 2, so that nothing downstream has to convert it. Present only on a column that also has `unit_column`, which already names where the unit comes from; this adds the two things `unit_column` does not say — which conversion applies, and what the value is left in.

conversion.description: `rate` — a quantity PER unit-period, normalized with public.rate_to_weekly. `duration` — a LENGTH of time, normalized with public.duration_to_weeks. They are NOT inverses: a duration of 1 month is ~4.35 weeks, a rate of 1 per month is ~0.23 per week, which is why the kind has to be stated and cannot be inferred from the unit.

canonical.description: The unit the promoted value is in. `ingest_apply_run` writes it into `unit_column`, so the tier-2 row STATES its unit rather than leaving a reader to know a default (§5 T1).

unit_column.description: Required when unit_source is 'column': which column names the unit.

meaning.description: What the value IS, in the user's terms — not a restatement of the column name.

grain.description: 'level' — a standing quantity. 'rate' and 'event' are reserved (see $reserved).

computed_by_unreachable.description: WP 6.2 · §4 D118 · WHY the writer named in `computed_by` has no live call site. Absent means it has one, and `contract:check` R18 fails a `computed_by` whose writer it cannot find called anywhere in src/ or supabase/functions/. This exists because D118 was a value with the right SHAPE and the wrong content — `network_summary` declared `computed_by: combine-project` on five columns and that function never touches the table; the only statement that can insert a row is an RPC with ZERO call sites. A generator cannot catch that, and `computed_by` is load-bearing since D101 (graphHashCoverage.test.ts derives the computed-column set from it). So an unreachable writer is now a DECLARED fact with a reason, which the reference page prints, rather than a name a reader assumes is live.

computed_by.description: WP 5.2b · the analyzer or function that WRITES this column, where the column is an analysis OUTPUT rather than something a person supplied. Absent means it is not one. Declared here because "which columns are computed" is a data fact, and `single-source` (I1) says a data fact is authored exactly once: it was authored twice — as prose in each field's `note`, and as a literal Set named COMPUTED_COLUMNS inside graphHashCoverage.test.ts. Two lists that must agree with nothing comparing them is D21 and D22's shape, and the manual could not tell a reader which half of `network_nodes` they uploaded without becoming a third.

consumed_by.description: Where the engine reads it, traced by grep, e.g. 'project_map.py::_map_supply -> SupplierLink.cost'. null means NOT TRACED — and then `note` must say so. Never a guess.

transform.description: What happens to the value between the column and the engine field.

missing_default.description: What the engine uses when the column is NULL. I6: a fallback absent from this contract may not exist in code.

substitutions.description: Every point where a value the user did not supply can stand in for one they did. §5's transparency standard is built on this list being complete.

provenance.description: The vocabulary the grid already renders (policyGridUi.tsx), plus two reserved states.

csv_header.description: THE NAME THE USER TYPES. This is what closes D21: the legacy docs headed each entry with the engine's name while the user types something else. null means the column has no CSV origin (a surrogate id, a timestamp, a server-set column).

required.description: Must the CSV carry it for the upload to be accepted?

validate.description: The rule the value must satisfy at ingestion, in a sentence a person reads.

rule.description: The SAME rule, in a form a validator can execute (WP 3.2). `validate` is the sentence and this is the check; the two are not allowed to disagree, and the point of having both is that the prose was the only version for three phases and nothing could run it. Absent means the column carries no machine-checkable rule yet.

kind.description: `unit` is a token public.unit_days() knows — the ONE unit table, never a list restated here (D10).

values.description: For kind `enum`: the accepted values, lowercased.

blank.description: What an empty cell means. `null` lands no value and is the contract's default for an optional column; `reject` is a row-level finding, which is what D7 asks for on a required numeric.

surfaces.description: COLUMN-GRAIN lineage: pages that name this field in an explicit select list. Filled by WP 5.1. Table-grain reach lives on the TABLE's own `surfaces`, because 'this page reads this table' is a fact about the table and repeating it on 30 columns is a fact authored 30 times (I1).

resolution.description: How a value for this field is decided when more than one source could supply it. Authored in WP 1.3 for engine-consumed fields; null elsewhere.

estimable_from.description: An EMPTY array is a positive statement, not an omission: this value may never be estimated. consumption_rate, moq and capacity_per_week are engineering facts, and a distribution fitted to one is a lie with error bars.

hybrid.description: null means the engine has no variability field for this quantity — see the RFC in PLAN.md §14. Do not invent one here.

page.description: The file in src/pages that reaches this data, e.g. `DataManager.tsx`.

via.description: How: `table read`, or `rpc <name>` when the hop goes through a SECURITY DEFINER function. An `.rpc()` names a function, not a table; recording which one is the difference between lineage and a list of RPC names.

grain.description: `column` — the field is named in an explicit `.select('a,b')` on a chain whose own `.from()` is this table; a reviewer can open the evidence line and see it. `table` — the page reaches the table at the evidence line, and whether THIS column is rendered is not established. `shell` — every module providing the read is reachable from ≥80% of pages, i.e. auth/session plumbing rather than a place this data is shown. The three are never blurred: claiming column grain on table evidence is the 'worse than none' case WP 5.1's brief names.

evidence.description: `path:line` of the access, relative to the repo root. `contract:check` R12 re-opens it and fails if no matching access is there — so a lineage entry cannot quietly go stale the way §4's citations did (D21, D22).

confirmed.description: A person read the evidence line and agreed. WP 5.1's brief: an unconfirmed lineage entry is worse than none, because it will be trusted. `false` publishes as UNCONFIRMED rather than as lineage.

note.description: Why this entry is qualified — e.g. the RPC reads the table but the page renders a verdict rather than the rows.
